argv:
A Meridian-3 has stopped reporting. How long can it keep working
offline, and how would I detect that from the Fleet Control API?

parsed.answer:
A Meridian-3 can keep working offline for up to **12 minutes** — the fixed offline autonomy window buffered in firmware. When the buffered queue is exhausted or the window ends (whichever comes first), the robot performs a safe-park. This window is not configurable. [sample_corpus/product-specs.md:Acme Robotics — Product Specifications > Meridian-3 Autonomous Mobile Robot > Offline Autonomy]

To detect this from the Fleet Control API:

1. **Watch `link_state`**: poll `GET /robots/{robot_id}/telemetry`. A value of `offline` means no report has been received for more than 30 seconds. [sample_corpus/api-reference.md:Fleet Control API Reference > Fleet Telemetry > GET /robots/{robot_id}/telemetry]

2. **Track `offline_seconds`**: this field counts up from the last successful report. When it crosses 12 minutes (720 seconds), a safe-park has almost certainly occurred — the robot makes that call on board, so Fleet Control cannot confirm it while the robot is offline. [sample_corpus/api-reference.md:Fleet Control API Reference > Fleet Telemetry > GET /robots/{robot_id}/telemetry] [sample_corpus/product-specs.md:Acme Robotics — Product Specifications > Meridian-3 Autonomous Mobile Robot > Offline Autonomy]

3. **Listen for webhooks**: you'll first receive a `robot.link_lost` event and see `link_state` flip to `offline`. On reconnect, `robot.link_restored` fires, and if the robot did safe-park, a `robot.safe_parked` event follows and `beacon` reads `amber`. [sample_corpus/faq.md:Frequently Asked Questions > Fleet Operations > What happens during a network outage?]

4. **Amber beacon persistence**: if the beacon stays amber for more than one minute after the link returns, the robot needs a physical check. [sample_corpus/support-runbook.md:Support Runbook > Many Robots Offline at Once]
